prior_gaps.description: Structured gap representations remain insufficiently validated for temporal constraints, multi-entity joins, and complex compositional evidence requirements; the corpus contains structured-gap, temporal-retrieval, and query-planning methods, but no admitted study evaluates these capabilities together.
prior_gaps.suggested_search_query: "structured evidence gap" temporal constraints multi-entity joins compositional retrieval iterative RAG
prior_gaps.resolution_notes: Still open after rounds 1-3. S2G-RAG provides a structured target/slot/description representation, while temporal retrieval and compositional planning are addressed separately, but the admitted evidence does not validate one structured-gap representation across temporal constraints, multi-entity joins, and complex compositional evidence requirements.

prior_gaps.description: No admitted study validates an iterative evidence-gap retrieval loop that jointly preserves document-version lineage, freshness or effective-time validity, and structured sufficiency decisions.
prior_gaps.suggested_search_query: "version-aware retrieval" temporal provenance iterative RAG document lineage freshness effective-time sufficiency
prior_gaps.resolution_notes: Still open after rounds 1-3. VersionRAG, Temporal GraphRAG, TimelyRAG, and S2G-RAG cover relevant version, temporal, or sufficiency functions in separate systems, but no admitted study evaluates one iterative loop that maintains lineage and effective-time validity while repeatedly deciding structured evidence sufficiency.

prior_gaps.description: Stopping reliability under domain shift remains open: sufficiency, confidence, conformal, and stability signals guide stopping in separate studies, but no admitted study provides a general bounded-risk iterative-RAG stopping guarantee under distribution shift.
prior_gaps.suggested_search_query: "iterative RAG" calibrated stopping domain shift conformal risk control selective prediction adaptive retrieval
prior_gaps.resolution_notes: Still open after rounds 1-3. The synthesis found calibrated adaptive stopping, conformal or risk-control methods under shift, and empirical iterative-RAG stopping studies, but no admitted work combines an iterative-RAG stopping rule with a bounded-risk guarantee that remains valid under distribution shift.

prior_gaps.description: The corpus does not test a bounded replenishment loop in which unauthorized candidates are filtered through native IAM, evidence sufficiency is reassessed, and another permission-constrained query is issued when authorized evidence remains incomplete.
prior_gaps.resolution_notes: Resolve by implementing a bounded controller around a real IAM-aware retrieval layer: retrieve candidates, apply native authorization checks before evidence exposure, reassess structured sufficiency using only authorized evidence, issue a follow-up permission-constrained query when gaps remain, and terminate on sufficiency or explicit budget bounds. Validate with integration tests covering mixed authorization, revoked access, partial evidence, and repeated replenishment.

prior_gaps.description: The evaluated systems do not jointly distinguish empty retrieval, authorization denial, unavailable source, unsupported extraction, exhausted budget, and true negative evidence as separate terminal or retry conditions.
prior_gaps.resolution_notes: Resolve by defining an explicit controller outcome/state taxonomy and implementing typed result codes for empty retrieval, authorization denial, source unavailable, extraction unsupported, budget exhausted, and verified negative evidence. Specify retry versus terminal transitions for each state and test them with deterministic fault injection, mocked access-control failures, unreachable sources, unsupported formats, exhausted budgets, and known-negative fixtures.

prior_gaps.description: An end-to-end cost evaluation covering retrieval calls, retrieved passages or tokens, planner or judge inference, reranking, permission-check latency, and total wall-clock latency remains absent from the admitted corpus.
prior_gaps.resolution_notes: Resolve with an instrumented benchmark harness that records per-request retrieval-call count, passages and tokens retrieved, planner and judge model tokens or monetary cost, reranker invocations and latency, authorization-check count and latency, retries, cache effects, and end-to-end wall-clock latency. Report component-level and aggregate distributions over representative workloads and compare fixed-budget and adaptive controllers.

prior_gaps.description: The corpus lacks a workplace-communication evaluation combining explicit evidence gaps with heterogeneous messages and documents, multi-hop dependencies, permission restrictions, stale or conflicting evidence, and bounded retrieval.
prior_gaps.resolution_notes: Resolve by constructing or curating a workplace-communication benchmark containing email or chat threads, attachments and structured documents, explicit answerable evidence gaps, multi-hop dependencies, ACL or IAM metadata, historical and superseded versions, stale and conflicting evidence, and defined retrieval budgets. Create gold evidence sets and state transitions, then evaluate completeness, provenance correctness, authorization compliance, temporal/version correctness, stopping behavior, abstention, and cost.

prior_gaps.description: No admitted study validates a single controller that jointly handles structured evidence gaps, permission-aware source access, version lineage, temporal validity, calibrated stopping, abstention, and total-cost budgeting; the reported successes remain component-level or cover smaller subsets of these functions.
prior_gaps.suggested_search_query: "adaptive RAG controller" permission-aware provenance temporal version calibrated stopping abstention budget
prior_gaps.resolution_notes: Still open after rounds 1-3. The admitted literature supplies component-level evidence for structured-gap retrieval, temporal or version-aware retrieval, permission filtering, calibrated stopping, abstention, and budget control, but no admitted paper evaluates all of these functions jointly in one controller.
